title: Why I'm Not Buying Duolingo Stock (Yet)
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; captions readable
summary: Parkevtate reiterates HOLD on Duolingo — he is not buying yet. Management's response to the AI threat is to prioritize customer acquisition over monetization: more freemium features to pull users into the ecosystem, targeting 100M daily active users over the next couple of years. Revenue grew from ~$100M (2020) to over $1.15B TTM; operating margin soared from -30% (2022) to a record 14.2% (a pattern he notes across 2022-restructuring tech names like Salesforce and UiPath), though the freemium pivot will likely stall or reverse margin expansion, and ROIC has already slid from ~40% toward 30% (still >2x WACC). The stock recovered from ~$89 in April to $143, trading at a 19x forward PE near its all-time low. His DCF fair value is $149 vs $143 — fairly valued to slightly undervalued — but he requires a 5-10% margin of safety (larger for DUOL's elevated risk), so he waits for a better entry. Thesis: fairly valued with elevated AI-disruption risk; wait. Bull case: the acquisition pivot works, ROIC rebounds above its prior peak. Bear case: AI and big-tech language tools reduce the need to learn languages; the freemium push compresses record margins. Call: DUOL HOLD (reiterated) at $143. No flip — no prior parkevtate call on DUOL.
